title: Characterized subgroups on the unit circle
summary: Given an ideal $\mathcal{I}$ on $ω$, a subgroup $H$ of the unit circle $\mathbb{T}$ is said to be $\mathcal{I}$-characterized if there exists an integer sequence $a=(a_n: n \in ω)$ such that $$ H=\mathsf{H}_{a}(\mathcal{I}):= \left\{x\in\mathbb{T}:\mathcal I\text{-}\lim_{n\to \infty} a_nx=0\right\}. $$ We also consider the corresponding $\mathcal{I}^\star$-version. We provide upper bounds for the topological complexities of those subgroups in terms of the complexity of $\mathcal{I}$.
